results.desc: fn defined BEFORE posix, then posix turned on: fn survives?
results.script: eval(){ echo FN; }; set -o posix; eval "echo SPECIAL"

results.desc: already-ON (fn predefined), side effect rewrites POSIXLY_CORRECT
results.script: eval(){ echo FN; }; set -o posix; A=$((POSIXLY_CORRECT=1)) eval "echo SPECIAL"

results.desc: flip-OFF attempt via command-sub unset (subshell: must NOT flip off)
results.script: eval(){ echo FN; }; POSIXLY_CORRECT=1; A=$(unset POSIXLY_CORRECT; echo x) eval "echo SPECIAL"

results.desc: is flip-OFF reachable from a prefix expansion at all? (arith cannot unset)
results.script: eval(){ echo FN; }; POSIXLY_CORRECT=1; A=$((POSIXLY_CORRECT=0)) eval "echo SPECIAL"; echo "pc=[${POSIXLY_CORRECT-UNSET}]"; shopt -qo posix && echo posix-ON || echo posix-OFF

results.desc: POSIXLY_CORRECT=0 name-level prefix still flips ON (presence counts)
results.script: eval(){ echo FN; }; unset POSIXLY_CORRECT; POSIXLY_CORRECT=0 eval "echo SPECIAL"

results.desc: fn shadowing 'break' inside a loop
